requirement:
A tool result containing text the harness redacted under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.redaction` MUST include a note saying that
`[REDACTED:<kind>]` replaces credential-shaped text and that the original is not
available. A result with no redacted text MUST NOT include the note.
rationale:
The `{test}` item `src/authoring/tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[only_results_with_redacted_text_carry_the_redaction_note]` covers both obligations in `requirements.authoring.redaction_notice`.

**Obligation 1: a result with redacted text MUST include a note.**
- The note must say that `[REDACTED:<kind>]` replaces credential-shaped text and that the original is not available.
- A source file containing a GitHub token is read with `habeas` (file and item). The result contains `[REDACTED:`. The test asserts that `note` contains both "[REDACTED:<kind>] replaces credential-shaped text" and "the original text is not available".
- A `ripgrep` search over the same file is asserted to carry `note == REDACTION_NOTE`.
- Requirement text and definition text containing a token are read through `habeas` with the `requirements` and `definition` forms. These results name no file. The test asserts that the token is absent, that `[REDACTED:` is present, and that `note == REDACTION_NOTE`.
- `src/authoring/tools.rs#fn[dispatch_paged]` applies `with_redaction_note` to every read tool's delivery. The `ripgrep` and `habeas` cases therefore exercise the same code path that other tools use, such as `ast_grep`.
- `src/authoring/pages.rs#mod[tests]/fn[redacted_results_reserve_space_for_the_note_on_every_delivered_page]` also asserts the note on every delivered page of a paged result. That test is not a `{test}` reference to this requirement, but it does not leave a gap here.

**Obligation 2: a result with no redacted text MUST NOT include the note.**
- A plain item (`fn[plain]`) from the same file has no `note`.
- Source whose own text contains `[REDACTED:kind]` was never redacted. The test asserts that the marker appears and that there is no `note`.
- Requirement text that literally contains the marker has no `note`.

These negative cases target the heuristic in `src/authoring/tools.rs#fn[needs_redaction_note]`, which compares marker lines against the original source. A naive "contains the marker" check would fail them.

I found no unacknowledged gap, so I chose true.

text: A tool result containing text the harness redacted under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.redaction` MUST include a note saying that
`[REDACTED:<kind>]` replaces credential-shaped text and that the original is not
available. A result with no redacted text MUST NOT include the note.
Habeas MUST apply the SDK's built-in credential rules to source text supplied
in mandatory inputs, tool reads, and search results, and to source text shown
in the book and `habeas info`. The same rules apply to configuration files.
Each match of a built-in `secretshape` rule MUST be replaced with
`[REDACTED:<rule name>]`, preserving every line break. The match MUST extend
through adjacent regions flagged by the entropy heuristic when only whitespace
separates them. Entropy alone MUST NOT trigger a replacement.
Outlines MUST use the original source for structure and spans. Structural
hashes MUST use the redacted text for each matched region as specified in
pinned exactly because changes to its rules can affect evidence hashes.
